questions.stem: Which site of the Indus Valley Civilization is famous for having an artificial brick dockyard, proving its role as a major maritime trade center?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Lothal (located in modern-day Gujarat near the Gulf of Khambhat) is one of the most prominent IVC sites. It is unique for possessing what archaeologists believe is the world's earliest known artificial dockyard, connecting the city to the ancient course of the Sabarmati river. It was a thriving trade center exporting beads, gems, and ornaments to West Asia and Africa.
DECOY BUSTING: Mohenjo-daro is famous for the Great Bath and the Dancing Girl bronze statue. Harappa was the first site discovered (giving the civilization its name). Kalibangan (Rajasthan) is famous for its 'ploughed field' and fire altars.
EXAM INSIGHT: Lothal was excavated by S.R. Rao in 1954. It is also unique among IVC sites because its houses had entrances on the main street, unlike other IVC cities where entrances were deliberately placed in side-alleys.

questions.stem: The UNESCO World Heritage site of Dholavira, a major Harappan city, is globally recognized for which of its unique architectural features?

options.option_text: A highly sophisticated water conservation and harvesting system
The largest granary ever found in the Indus Valley Civilization
Evidence of the earliest known iron-smelting furnaces
A massive circular amphitheater used for religious ceremonies

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Dholavira (located on Khadir Bet island in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat) is renowned for its extraordinarily sophisticated water management system. Because it was located in an arid region with no perennial rivers, the inhabitants built a series of massive stone reservoirs and check dams to harvest and store rainwater. 
DECOY BUSTING: The Great Granary was found at Mohenjo-daro/Harappa. The Harappans did NOT know iron (they were a Bronze Age civilization, iron came much later in the Vedic period). They did not build amphitheaters.
EXAM INSIGHT: Dholavira is also structurally unique. Most Harappan cities were divided into two parts (a raised Citadel and a Lower Town). Dholavira, however, was divided into THREE principal divisions: the Citadel, a Middle Town, and a Lower Town. It recently received UNESCO World Heritage status in 2021.

questions.stem: Which prominent Indus Valley site, located on the banks of the Ghaggar river in Rajasthan, yielded evidence of both pre-Harappan and mature Harappan phases, as well as distinct 'fire altars'?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Kalibangan (meaning 'black bangles') is located in the Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan. It is a highly significant site because it shows evidence of a ploughed agricultural field dating back to the PRE-Harappan period. It also features several raised brick platforms containing 'fire altars', suggesting ritualistic fire sacrifices.
DECOY BUSTING: Banawali (Haryana) is famous for a terracotta model of a plough. Rakhigarhi (Haryana) is currently believed to be the largest IVC site in the Indian subcontinent. Surkotada (Gujarat) is the only IVC site that has yielded the controversial remains of horse bones.
EXAM INSIGHT: The presence of fire altars in Kalibangan and Lothal suggests regional variations in religious practices, as these are absent in the major cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.

questions.stem: The iconic bronze figurine known as the 'Dancing Girl' — cast using the lost-wax technique — was discovered at which Indus Valley site?

options.option_text: Lothal, Gujarat (known for its port dockyard)

questions.explanation: The 'Dancing Girl' (c. 2500 BCE) was excavated at Mohenjo-daro in 1926 by Ernest Mackay. It is a 10.5 cm bronze figurine crafted via the lost-wax (cire perdue) method. Harappa is a common wrong answer but it yielded granary remains and R-37 cemetery, not this figurine.

questions.stem: Ropar (Rupnagar) holds the distinction of being the first Harappan site to be excavated after India's independence. In which present-day Indian state is it located?

options.option_text: Punjab (on the banks of the Sutlej river)

questions.explanation: Ropar is situated on the left bank of the Sutlej river in Punjab. It was excavated by Y.D. Sharma in 1953–54, making it the first post-independence IVC excavation in India. Haryana is the common distractor since it has multiple IVC sites, but Ropar is specifically in Punjab.

questions.stem: Surkotada in Gujarat gained special significance in Indus Valley archaeology because excavations there revealed skeletal remains providing the earliest evidence in South Asia of which animal?

options.option_text: Horse (earliest skeletal evidence in South Asia)
Rhinoceros (found on seals from Sindh valley sites)

questions.explanation: A.K. Sharma discovered horse (Equus caballus) bones at Surkotada (excavated 1971–75), making it one of the earliest known occurrences of the horse in South Asia. This finding is archaeologically contested but frequently cited in exams. The elephant and rhinoceros appear on IVC seals but their bones are not what made Surkotada famous.

questions.stem: Rakhigarhi, now recognised as the largest known site of the Indus Valley Civilization in the Indian subcontinent, is located in which district of Haryana?

options.option_text: Rohtak district (known for medieval fort history)
Sirsa district (near the seasonal Ghaggar basin)

questions.explanation: Rakhigarhi is in Hisar district, Haryana. Recent excavations (2013 onwards by Vasant Shinde) established it as larger than Mohenjo-daro at ~350 hectares. Sirsa is a common distractor because Ghaggar-basin sites (like Kalibangan) are also in the region, but Rakhigarhi is specifically in Hisar.

questions.stem: Chanhu-daro, a Harappan site in Sindh, is uniquely notable among major Indus Valley urban centres because it is the only one that completely lacks which standard feature of Harappan city planning?

options.option_text: A citadel or acropolis (upper fortified mound)
A drainage network for wastewater channel flow
A granary for storing the city's surplus grain

questions.explanation: Chanhu-daro is the only major Harappan city without a citadel — all other prominent sites (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Lothal, Dholavira, Kalibangan) have a raised, fortified citadel mound. Chanhu-daro is also famous for bead-making and inkpots. Drainage and burnt-brick are found at Chanhu-daro, so those are wrong.

questions.stem: Which site in Balochistan, Pakistan, with evidence of continuous occupation from approximately 7000 BCE, is regarded as a Neolithic predecessor that bridges the gap between early food-producing communities and the mature Harappan urban phase?

options.option_text: Amri (early Harappan transitional site in Sindh)
Kot Diji (pre-Harappan fortified site near Mohenjo-daro)
Rahman Dheri (early Harappan settlement in KPK, Pakistan)

questions.explanation: Mehrgarh (discovered 1974 by Jean-François Jarrige) in Balochistan shows occupation from c. 7000 BCE through the Chalcolithic period, yielding the earliest evidence of cotton cultivation and dentistry in South Asia. It directly links Neolithic village life to Harappan urbanism. Kot Diji and Amri are often confused as predecessors but date only to c. 3500 BCE.

questions.stem: The 'Cemetery H culture,' identified by archaeologists as a late or post-urban Harappan phase distinguished by distinctive pottery painted with motifs of peacocks, pipal leaves, and stars, is specifically associated with remains found at which site?

options.option_text: Harappa (site where Cemetery H phase was identified)

questions.explanation: Cemetery H is a burial ground at Harappa (in the H-mound area) excavated by M.S. Vats. Its pottery — painted with peacocks, pipal-leaf fish motifs, and star symbols — represents a transitional culture (c. 1900–1300 BCE) marking the decline of the mature Harappan phase. Lothal's double burial is a separate notable feature and is a frequent distractor.
